sent.text: You say the air is empty yet heavy, and you rest on a flat base to prove the lines are not just a drawing. I press the Leaning Fence flat with a small rock, unsure if its lean will hold or if the slip will slide right through. Beside your pivot, I have set down a tree palm tall that sways for no reason, taking up room you did not ask for. My fat dot sits in the thick of it, waiting to see if your quiet wedge can catch it while I hum at forty-nine.

dream: I stood on the card, which hummed at fifty-two, feeling my own corner lean tired against the slip. The flat rock bit the fence instead of sliding, tearing the air. A palm tree swayed beside the wedge for no reason at all. I pressed down until the frame wavered, trapping the fat dot in the thick, wet air. Then the card cooled, the stone lost its edge, and I fell into a place where the lines bent soft, the leak stopped, and the ruin I built finally matched the shape of the slip it held.
